title: Network feasibility may require removing a constrained node rather than relaxing one link
source_unit: NBER Working Paper 35757, a theoretical graph model of spectrum repacking, station buyouts, and pairwise engineering waivers
geography: Conceptual spectrum-market and network-design mechanism; no observed U.S. auction or station outcome sample

node_removal.value: Buying out any one station can reduce the number of channels needed in the model

single_edge_relaxation.value: Relaxing any one interference restriction need not reduce the channels needed

general_result.value: For every k at least 4, some k-vertex-critical graph has no critical edge

observations.method: Graph model representing stations as vertices and pairwise interference restrictions as edges; the paper combines a construction resolving a graph-theoretic conjecture with implications for spectrum-repacking market design.
observations.uncertainty: This is a theoretical result, not an estimate of auction prices, station value, consumer access, broadcaster exit, or realized channel availability. The translation from graph feasibility to a particular regulatory proceeding requires engineering, legal, financial, and public-interest evidence.
observations.subgroup: Modeled stations/vertices and interference restrictions/edges in k-vertex-critical networks; no observed station subgroup is estimated.
observations.counterinterpretation: A buyout can impose concentration, service, employment, local-media, or public-interest costs. Relaxing multiple edges, redesigning technology, sharing spectrum, or changing geographic assignments may be better in a real system even when a single-edge audit fails.

boundary: This record adds a network-remedy-design mechanism: local link-by-link relaxation can miss node-level complementarity. It does not establish a realized spectrum remedy, consumer benefit, broadcaster outcome, market concentration effect, or U.S. policy success.
